description: Implement the muntutils program in BOTH C and C++ (explicit user requirement). Split: the filesystem walk / size-measurement / artifact-classification core in C (mirroring tools/size/size.c style), and the source-analysis + reachability + trimming engine in C++17. muntutils is a single binary with subcommands for its two capabilities: (1) SAFE-BY-DEFAULT source trimmer that determines statically (and best-effort dynamically) which functions are actually reachable/called across the source tree and emits a slimmed representation into a SEPARATE output tree, and (2) size/stats reporting that measures raw source, slimmed source, and compiled artifacts and generates a dual-audience report. This is one coherent implementation unit.
steps: Create tools/muntutils/muntutils_fs.h and tools/muntutils/muntutils_fs.c (C11). The C core provides: recursive directory enumeration (model on tools/size/size.c: POSIX lstat/opendir/readdir; do not follow symlinks; guard Windows with _WIN32 using the same Win32 Unicode enumeration pattern as size.c), logical file-size summation with saturating uint64 (reuse the add_u64 idiom), file classification by extension into RAW SOURCE (.c .cc .cpp .cxx .h .hpp .hxx and similar) vs COMPILED ARTIFACT (.so .dll .a .o .dylib and extensionless executables where detectable), and helpers to write bytes + IEC human-readable units (reuse the print_human idiom). Expose a C-linkage API (guarded with extern "C" in the header) so the C++ TU can call it: e.g. functions to sum sizes of a tree filtered by category and to enumerate source files into a caller-provided callback.

Create tools/muntutils/muntutils_trim.hpp and tools/muntutils/muntutils_trim.cpp (C++17). Implement the source-analysis + reachability + trimming engine: (a) parse each C/C++ source file with a pragmatic lexer/heuristic scanner (not a full compiler): identify top-level function DEFINITIONS (name + brace-balanced body span) and record all IDENTIFIER references / call sites across the whole tree; (b) build a call/reference graph and compute reachability from a set of roots. Roots MUST be conservative: main, any function whose ADDRESS IS TAKEN (referenced without a following call paren), symbols referenced via dlsym/GetProcAddress-style string usage (best-effort string scan), functions with common entry attributes/exports if detectable, and by default treat externally-linkable (non-static) functions as potentially-reachable unless a strict flag is set. (c) A function is classified DEAD only when it is provably unreferenced under these conservative rules; when uncertain, KEEP it. (d) Emit the slimmed representation: for each source file, write a copy into the output tree with dead functions removed (or replaced by a clearly commented stub marker) while preserving includes, macros, types, and everything not confidently dead. Track per-file and total confidence and an explicit list of what could not be resolved (function pointers, dynamic dispatch, preprocessor-conditional bodies, etc.).

SAFETY (authoritative, user-approved): default invocation MUST NOT overwrite or delete originals. The trim subcommand REQUIRES an explicit output directory and writes the slim tree there only. In-place rewriting is allowed ONLY behind an explicit opt-in flag (--in-place, accept --apply as an alias), and even then each file rewritten MUST first be copied to a backup (e.g. <file>.bak) before it is modified. A bare/default run must never touch original source. Refuse to run in-place without the explicit flag and refuse if a backup cannot be created.

Implement the size/stats report (capability 2) using the C core for measurement and C++ for formatting. The report MUST include: raw source stats (file count + total bytes, per major category), slimmed source stats (produced from the trim output tree), and compiled-artifact stats (.so/.dll/.a/.o/executables sizes). It MUST contain BOTH a plain-language summary understandable by a non-specialist adult user AND a detailed numbers section for a programmer. Emit it as a clean text/markdown artifact to a path the user names (stdout if none given). State clearly that raw-vs-slim source comparison is a source-size estimate and that compiled-artifact sizes are measured separately.

Wire subcommands in a main.cpp (C++17, links the C core). Provide: `muntutils trim <src-tree> --out <dir> [--in-place|--apply] [--strict]`, `muntutils report <src-tree> [--slim <dir>] [--out <report>]`, plus `--help` and `--version` (version 1.00) matching the size/limit help/version style. main.cpp orchestrates: analyze -> (plan/emit slim into out tree) -> measure -> report, honoring safe-by-default semantics.

Put the NCSU attribution line EXACTLY as 'Program based on Science at NCSU - Max Rupplin - MEARVK LLC 2026.' in the header comment block of each new source file, alongside (not replacing) existing MEARVK provenance framing used by size/limit. Frame it as a science/attribution statement, not a legal-ownership or execution-authorization claim. Avoid em dashes in prose comments (flag names and numeric ranges are fine).

Compile locally to validate as you go using the system fallback: `g++ -std=c++17 -Wall -Wextra -Werror -O2 -c muntutils_trim.cpp main.cpp` and `gcc -std=c11 -Wall -Wextra -Werror -O2 -c muntutils_fs.c`, then link with g++ into ./muntutils. Fix all warnings (the build treats them as errors).
acceptance_criteria: tools/muntutils/ contains C sources (muntutils_fs.c/.h, C11) AND C++ sources (muntutils_trim.cpp/.hpp and main.cpp, C++17); both languages are genuinely used (C core called from C++ via extern "C").
The whole thing compiles clean with -std=c11 / -std=c++17 -Wall -Wextra -Werror -O2 using system gcc/g++ and links into a ./muntutils binary.
`./muntutils --version` prints version 1.00; `./muntutils --help` lists the trim and report subcommands.

Capability 1: a default `muntutils trim <src> --out <dir>` writes a slim tree into <dir> and leaves every original file byte-identical (verifiable by checksum/diff). Running trim without --out (or attempting in-place without the explicit flag) does not modify originals.
In-place: `muntutils trim <src> --in-place` (or --apply) rewrites files but first creates a .bak backup of each rewritten file; refuses/aborts safely if a backup cannot be made.
Reachability is conservative: functions of uncertain reachability are KEPT, and the tool reports its confidence and an explicit list of constructs it could not resolve.

Capability 2: `muntutils report <src> --slim <dir>` produces a text/markdown report containing raw source stats, slimmed source stats, and compiled-artifact stats, with both a plain-language summary and a detailed programmer section.
verification: Compile: `gcc -std=c11 -Wall -Wextra -Werror -O2 -c muntutils_fs.c` and `g++ -std=c++17 -Wall -Wextra -Werror -O2 -c muntutils_trim.cpp main.cpp`, then link into ./muntutils; confirm exit code 0 and no warnings.

Create a throwaway sample tree (e.g. /tmp/muntutils-sample) with a .c/.cpp file containing a used function called from main and an obviously-unused static helper; run `./muntutils trim /tmp/muntutils-sample --out /tmp/muntutils-out`; confirm originals are byte-identical (sha256sum before/after match) and /tmp/muntutils-out contains a slim copy with the dead static helper removed/stubbed and the used function retained.
Copy the sample to /tmp/muntutils-inplace and run `./muntutils trim /tmp/muntutils-inplace --in-place`; confirm a .bak exists for each rewritten file.

Run `./muntutils report /tmp/muntutils-sample --slim /tmp/muntutils-out --out /tmp/muntutils-report.md`; confirm the report contains raw stats, slim stats, compiled-artifact section, a plain-language summary, and a programmer numbers section.
findings: Implemented tools/muntutils with 5 source files: muntutils_fs.h/.c (C11 filesystem walk, size measurement, artifact classification, extern "C" API), muntutils_trim.hpp/.cpp (C++17 heuristic scanner + conservative reachability + slimming engine), and main.cpp (C++17 CLI orchestrating trim/report). Both languages genuinely used: the C++ engine calls the C core mu_measure_tree/mu_enumerate_sources via extern "C". All compile clean with gcc -std=c11 and g++ -std=c++17 under -Wall -Wextra -Werror -O2 (system gcc/g++ 11.5.0). Attribution string 'Program based on Science at NCSU - Max Rupplin - MEARVK LLC 2026.' present in all 5 file headers alongside MEARVK provenance framing; no em dashes in prose. VERIFICATION PASSED: (1) safe-by-default trim writes slim tree to --out and leaves originals byte-identical (sha256 verified); dead static helpers dead_helper/another_dead removed via clearly commented stub markers, used_helper/main/exported_util kept. Slim app.c recompiled and ran correctly (output 42). (2) trim without --out and no --in-place refuses with exit 1. (3) --in-place created <file>.bak backups byte-identical to originals before rewriting; engine aborts safely if a backup cannot be written. (4) --strict additionally trims the non-static exported_util. (5) report --slim --out produces markdown with raw source stats, slim source stats, compiled-artifact stats, a plain-language 'Summary for everyone' section, and a 'Details for a programmer' section; report to stdout works when --out omitted. (6) --version prints 'muntutils 1.00'; --help lists trim and report. NOTES / HONEST LIMITS: reachability is deliberately tree-wide-conservative (any named reference anywhere keeps a function; duplicate-named functions kept; non-static kept unless --strict); the engine reports confidence and an explicit unresolved list (preprocessor conditionals, function pointers, dynamic dispatch, dlopen/dlsym). Stubbing (not deletion) means a trimmed file can occasionally be slightly larger than the original when a leading comment plus stub text exceeds the removed body; the report handles the slim>=raw case gracefully and states the comparison is an estimate. IMPORTANT for FEAT-003: I did NOT create build.sh/install.sh/Makefile/README/.hss/.hsss/1-2-3-4.mmd, did NOT modify tools/Makefile, and did NOT commit; those are FEAT-003's scope. Left no .o files or binary in the tree (cleaned up after validation). A feature-test macro (_DEFAULT_SOURCE) is defined at the top of muntutils_fs.c so lstat/opendir compile under -std=c11 without relying on build.sh flags; FEAT-003's build.sh can keep or override this. Did not touch tools/pcopy (pre-existing unrelated build bug) or tools/pmove.
